host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ PRO 395 w/ Radeon 8060S

injected: nothing (own VAE draw, own diffusion noise, own negative LM)
seeding: each request is reseeded to base_seed + its index, so a request does not depend on how many requests ran before it

gates.voice_attribution: for a script with more than one speaker, the encoder's window assignment must reproduce the script's whole speaker sequence, not only its endpoints

limitations: The held-out axis is the script. Only the two voice sets the fixtures pin are used, because using any other voice file would mean reproducing the fork's WAV preprocessing (librosa 24 kHz resample plus its -25 dBFS normalizer) in-tree, and a subtly different reference is a subtly different request.

The random operands are the session's own: no recorded noise, negative condition or prompt embedding is injected. A request IS reproducible at a fixed seed, because the suite reseeds the session per request; it is not comparable to the torch lane, whose stream differs.
A seed does not align torch and HIP random streams, so this suite is not a torch comparison; it qualifies this lane's own output.

Voice attribution resolves speaker changes inside an utterance that contains both voices, not absolute voice identity: classifying single-voice audio against both references sits at the noise floor and is recorded as attribution_identity_control rather than gated.

The WER gate is measured by the same runtime it qualifies. The suite transcribes the reference implementation's own PCM as an evaluator floor, which bounds the ASR lane's systematic error, but a floor of 0.0 does not make every non-zero WER attributable to the TTS lane: the evaluator can still mishear audio whose phonetics differ from the reference. Separating those two needs an independent ASR on the same waveform, which this suite does not run.

evaluator_floor.method: the ASR lane transcribes the reference implementation's own PCM for the pinned requests (single_audio.npz / two_audio.npz), which contains every word; the WER it reports there is the evaluator's, not the TTS lane's

requests.transcript: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
I heard there is big news in text to speech lately. Yes, and it runs locally on this machine.

evaluator_floor.interpretation: a request whose WER is at or below max_wer is not evidence of a synthesis defect. A floor of 0.0 means the evaluator reads the reference implementation's audio exactly; it does NOT mean every non-zero WER on this lane's audio is a synthesis defect, because the evaluator can still mishear audio whose phonetics differ from the reference. Establishing that case needs an independent ASR on the same waveform

attribution_instrument.method: hipengine.runtime.vibevoice_encoder.encode_reference (deterministic, no VAE sampling); each window assigned to the reference voice with the higher cosine similarity to its mean latent
attribution_instrument.resolves: speaker changes inside an utterance that contains both voices: the 4-turn script reproduces [0, 1, 0, 1] on all three seeds
attribution_instrument.does_not_resolve: absolute voice identity for single-voice audio. Classifying a single-speaker request against both references sits at the noise floor (mean cosines 0.4236 against 0.4125 for one request), assigns every window to the wrong reference for another, and is therefore recorded per request as attribution_identity_control rather than gated
attribution_instrument.asr_speaker_labels: reported per request as a diagnostic, not gated: on these requests the ASR reports one speaker for two-speaker scripts that contain both voices

command: uv run --with jiwer --with transformers python scripts/vibevoice_tts_quality_suite.py --seeds 20260915,20260916,20260917,20260918,20260919,20260920,20260921,20260922,20260923,20260924 --work /tmp/vv-drift-quality-cfg-rowtile --out /tmp/vv-drift-quality-cfg-rowtile.json
